newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-MORE THAN LOCAL PRIDE AT STAKE IN BASQUE DERBY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MORE THAN LOCAL PRIDE AT STAKE IN BASQUE DERBY.

text.p: The heated verbal exchange which has preceded this weekend's Real Sociedad-Athletic Bilbao Spanish league game may, ironically, be an indication that for the first time in several years the encounter is just as important on the field as it is off.
With both clubs emerging from the doldrums, the Basque derby will be about UEFA Cup places, and not just fierce local pride.
Real are riding high in sixth, while Athletic are one place, and four points back.

Since the Spanish Cup -- and with it entry to next season's Cup Winners' Cup -- could end up in the hands of one of the lesser teams, sixth place may be the last to give access to European competition.
And the always tense relationship between the two clubs has heated up in recent days after Real manager Javier Irureta said that he would not shake hands with Athletic counterpart Luis Fernandez.
"You can wait until Monday, because I have a poem prepared," warned Athletic coach Luis Fernandez.
The outspoken former PSG manager used something other than poetry while crossing swords with half a dozen opposite numbers since moving back to Spain at the beginning of the season.
But Fernandez and his team earnt only praise from Racing Santander coach Marcos Alonso last Sunday, after an Athletic side down to just nine-men launched an epic comeback to earn a 2-2 draw.
Striker Ismael Urzaiz was again the hero of a characteristically gutsy performance from a side that seems finally to be emerging from a long decline.
As the star-studded Spanish league has imported more and more foreign talent, Athletic have suffered from their policy to stick by players born in the Basque country.
Until recently a similar policy existed down the coast at Real, whose San Sebastian home -- unlike the industrial city of Bilbao -- is an elegant resort town.
Real have gone half-way to scrapping the rule by signing foreigners but not non-Basque Spaniards.
And with Romanian Gheorghe Craioveanu, fellow striker Darko Kovacevic of Yugoslavia and Nigerian midfielder Mutiu Adepojo at the helm Real have blossomed this season.
Both sides are still some way from the glory days of the early 1980s, when Barcelona and Real Madrid went four years without a title as each Basque side snatched consecutive league championships.
But after years in which local pride seemed to be the only thing at stake, the clash once again has the look of one of the Spanish league's classic encounters.
